title: Integer identity
prompt: `Integer a = 1000; Integer b = 1000;` — what is `a == b`?
options: `false` (usually) — == compares references, and 1000 is outside the -128..127 cache
explanation: Autoboxing caches -128..127, so `Integer a = 100 == b` happens to be true — and then breaks at 1000. Never == boxed types; use .equals or unbox to int.

title: Silent overflow
options: A negative number — int overflow wraps around silently
explanation: 4×10⁹ exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (~2.1×10⁹), wrapping to -294967296. Java throws NOTHING for int overflow. When sums can exceed 2.1 billion, compute in long: `(long) x + x`.

title: The midpoint bug
prompt: In binary search, why write `int mid = l + (r - l) / 2;` instead of `(l + r) / 2`?
options: `l + r` can overflow int when both are large; `l + (r - l) / 2` cannot
explanation: With l and r both near 2 billion, l + r wraps negative and mid becomes garbage. This bug lived in the JDK's own binarySearch for nine years.

title: Negative modulo
options: `-1` — the result takes the sign of the dividend
explanation: Java's % is a remainder, not a mathematical modulo. For a guaranteed non-negative result (circular indexing!): `((a % b) + b) % b`.

title: The length gauntlet
prompt: Fill in the correct size access for each type — parentheses matter.
explanation: Array: field `.length`. String: method `.length()`. Collection: method `.size()`. Three APIs, three spellings — thanks, Java.

title: Mutating while iterating
prompt: `for (Integer x : list) { if (x < 0) list.remove(x); }` — what happens?
options: ConcurrentModificationException (typically) — you can't structurally modify a list inside its own for-each
explanation: Collect removals into a second list, use `list.removeIf(x -> x < 0)`, or iterate by index backwards.

title: Array default values
prompt: `new int[3]`, `new boolean[3]`, and `new Integer[3]` start filled with…
options: 0, false, and null respectively — and reading a null Integer into an int throws NPE
explanation: Primitives get zero-values; object arrays get null. `int x = integerArr[0];` on a fresh Integer[] is a NullPointerException at the unbox.

title: Concatenation cost
prompt: `String r = ""; for (...n times...) r += ch;` — total time?
options: O(n²) — each += copies the whole string so far; use StringBuilder for O(n)
explanation: 1 + 2 + ... + n copies ≈ n²/2. On a 10⁵-char build, that's the difference between instant and TLE.
